title: owo-lib issue #504: EdmOps throws a NullPointerException on null input instead of returning a DataResult error
licence: GitHub issue thread: user-generated content under the GitHub Terms of Service; the repo licence (MIT) does not cover issue text
text:
[issue by neonishere]
### Versions

- Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.248
- owo-lib 0.12.15.5-beta.1+1.21
- Accessories 1.1.0-beta.53+1.21.1
- Cold Sweat 2.4.3.1

### What happens

Putting armor that was insulated at Cold Sweat's sewing table into an Accessories cosmetic armor slot disconnects the player. The item stays in the slot, so the same packet is sent on every login and the player cannot rejoin until the save is edited.

reports of the same crash:

- wisp-forest/accessories#418
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#605
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#683
- Momo-Softworks/Cold-Sweat#699


```
Internal Exception: io.netty.handler.codec.DecoderException:
  Failed to decode packet 'clientbound/minecraft:custom_payload'
Caused by: java.lang.RuntimeException: Failed decoding custom payload accessories:main:
  io.wispforest.endec.impl.StructField$StructFieldException:
  Exception occurred when decoding a given StructField: [Field: dirtyCosmeticStacks]
Caused by: java.lang.NullPointerException:
  Cannot invoke "io.wispforest.endec.format.edm.EdmElement.value()" because "input" is null
    at io.wispforest.owo.serialization.format.edm.EdmOps.getStringValue(EdmOps.java:157)
    at com.mojang.serialization.Codec$16.read / PrimitiveCodec.decode
    at com.momosoftworks.coldsweat.data.codec.impl.ConfigData.decodeFromMap(ConfigData.java:99)
    at com.momosoftworks.coldsweat.data.codec.impl.ConfigData$1.decode(ConfigData.java:69)
    at io.wispforest.owo.serialization.CodecUtils.decodeWithCodecFromDeserializer(CodecUtils.java:98)
```

### Cause

`EdmOps.getStringValue` calls `input.value()` without checking `input`. The same goes for `getNumberValue`, `getBooleanValue`, `getByteBuffer`, `getStream` and `getMapValues` (the last two compare against `empty()` first and then call `input.value()`).

`NbtOps` and `JsonOps` use an `instanceof` check, so a null input gives them a `DataResult.error`. Some codecs depend on that. Cold Sweat reads optional keys like this:

```java
codec.decode(ops, input.get(key)).result().map(Pair::getFirst).orElse(defaultValue)
```

`MapLike.get` returns null for a missing key, the decode fails, and the default is used. With `EdmOps` the decode throws instead. In this case the missing keys are `registry_name` and `registry_key` inside the `cold_sweat:armor_insulation` component, which are only written when the insulator comes from a registry.

Passing null to a codec is arguably sloppy on Cold Sweat's side, but it works with the vanilla ops, so any mod that does the same will break whenever its data goes through `CodecUtils.toEndec`.

### Suggested fix

Return the existing error result when `input` is null in the read methods of `EdmOps`, for example:

```java
public DataResult<String> getStringValue(EdmElement<?> input) {
    if (input != null && input.value() instanceof String value) return DataResult.success(value);
    return DataResult.error(() -> "Not a string: " + input);
}
```
